scope.description: state flip-flops whose asynchronous control inputs are driven

findings.summary: 4 asynchronous control input(s) of the state register are driven by logic rather than tied to their inactive value. solve_fsm builds its next-state function from the gate library's next_state expression only, so these inputs do not appear in any recovered condition. Every transition below is conditional on them staying inactive.
findings.title: Asynchronous set/reset inputs are driven by logic and are not modelled

primitives.reason: the reset pin(s) of this flip-flop type are not part of the library's next-state function, and solve_fsm models only that function; an asynchronous clear or preset driven by real logic is therefore invisible in the recovered graph

unsupported.reason: asynchronous set/reset behaviour of the state flip-flops is outside the model solve_fsm uses

method.description: Every variable left in a recovered condition is resolved back to its net and classified: a primary input, or the output of a flip-flop outside the state register.
method.name: condition variable classification

scope.description: nets driven by flip-flops outside the state register that the transition conditions read

findings.summary: The transition relation is conditioned on n575, which dfrtp_2_29900_201280 drives. This is not necessarily wrong -- a controller may react to a counter -- but the recovered graph describes this register's behaviour *given* those signals, not a closed machine driven by inputs alone. If they were meant to be part of the machine, the state register selection is too small.
findings.title: The recovered conditions depend on 1 signal(s) from outside the state register

unsupported.reason: hal_fsm solves one state register at a time; a machine whose transitions depend on another register is only described relative to that register's outputs
